Hochzuverehrender Herr Hoffrath!

1800 rt. Zinsen bezahlt sind. Dan kan ich dort erscheinen und meinen Plan

Sie in der Verzweiflung nach der Auspfändung um der v. d.

mich der Fürst damit, den erscheine ich dort gerechtfertiget aber auch nicht ohne Citat. Ich führe dan mit Ehre meine Sache aus — Dismembrire einen Theil meiner Güter, weise meine Kinder die Zinßen zu ihrer Unterhaltung an und gehe dann zum König, wo ich bleibe bis vieles geschehen ist, dies ist mein Plan und dies sind die Folgen, was der Fürst Rath wegen den 1,800 rt schaft — Geschieht dies leztere nicht den kan ich dort nicht mehr auftreten sondern gehe nach Königsberg und von da vieleicht in der Hölle — Das Herz möchte mich bersten, wenn ich mein Unglück was ich so unverschuldet leide überdenke.

Schweinern kan mit 1,800 rt gerettet und ich im Stand gesezt werden alle Pläne auszuführen — Hier würde es auch Regenreiche Folge, bereiten. Mann würde schonender mit mich umgehen, wo ich Schweinern wieder frey hätte, also alles kömt dort auf die schleunige Hilfe sie Durchlaucht an Ich würde ihm ja gerne dafür wieder Lebeseeligkeit und alles opfern, wann der Herr nur dies für mich thut Sorgen Ewr Wohlgeborn, also wann es Ihnen in der Welt, möglich ist, und schaffen Sie bald Rath den kan ich den 12ten Sept. von hier abreisen um den 16ten in Schlawenschitz sein — ohne Diese Hülfe aber verlaste ich alles Mit danns baren Herzen, und wahrer Hochachtung werde ich stets sein

Euer Wohlgeborn

Kontop den 31ten August

1809.

translation.en:
61

Your Honour,

Highly Honoured Sir, Court Councillor!

Your Honour's most esteemed letter I received today by express, my joy was at first without bounds to know you as my weather in Wrocław, but on reading your friendly letter further, fresh sorrow stunned my heart, so that I could scarcely compose myself. I have a plan by which I may be rescued from all my embarrassments, only 1,800 Rthl of interest must be paid; before that I cannot come to Wrocław or into those parts. Honour and fortune are still not at stake there; I am for the present dreadfully disgraced by the one accursed v. d. Lahr affair, and cannot show myself there any sooner than when the 1,800 Rthl of interest are paid. Then I can appear there and carry out my plan. If the Most Serene Lord does not help me with this trifle, then may God stand by my forsaken children; I shall then go to another place, where I shall not require His Serene Highness's help. I have sent His Serene Highness the [uncertain: Bruß] of my daughter, which she wrote in despair, after the distraint over the v. d. Lahr debt, to my youngest son; and if such a cry of lamentation does not move the Lord, if he does not help me with the trifle, then all gentle feelings have ever been strangers to him. Dear friend — it is 1,800 Rthl that can save me from shame and mockery, indeed from ruin; these decide my choice or dwelling — I must have them, for before that I shall not come thither — If the Prince rescues

me therewith, then I appear there justified, but also not without citation. I then carry out my cause with honour — dismember a part of my estates, assign to my children the interest for their maintenance, and then go to the King, where I remain until much has been done. This is my plan, and these are the consequences, if the Prince provides counsel concerning the 1,800 Rthl — If this last does not happen, then I can no longer present myself there, but shall go to Königsberg and from there perhaps into hell — My heart would burst within me when I consider my misfortune, which I suffer so undeservedly.

Here the estates are sequestered, through the noise (bruit) which I endured in Berlin eternally of the Lahr affair; there, however, [uncertain: swum] — but where am I to turn? Świniary can be saved with 1,800 Rthl, and I be put in a position to carry out all my plans — Here too it would prepare rain-rich consequences. People would deal more sparingly with me if I had Świniary free again; thus everything there depends on the speedy help of His Serene Highness. I would gladly sacrifice for it in return [uncertain: Lebeseeligkeit] and all else, if only the Lord does this for me. Take care of it, Your Honour, then, if it is in any way in the world possible for you, and procure counsel soon, for then I can set out from here on the 12th of September so as to be in Sławięcice by the 16th — but without this help I abandon everything. With a thankful heart, and true high esteem, I shall ever be

Your Honour's

Konotop, the 31st of August

1809.

faithfully devoted friend and servant

v Triebenfeld

summary_en: The writer urgently asks a Court Councillor in Wrocław to obtain 1,800 Rthl from the Prince for interest now due. He says the v. d. Lahr affair has left him exposed and that his estates have been placed under sequestration. With 1,800 Rthl, he says, Świniary could be saved. Without help he says he will go to Königsberg; with it he could leave on 12 September and be in Sławięcice on the 16th.
summary_de: Der Schreiber bittet einen Hoffrath in Wrocław dringend, beim Fürsten 1800 Rthl für fällige Zinsen zu erwirken. Durch die v. d. Lahrsche Geschichte sei er bloßgestellt, und seine Güter seien sequestriert. Mit 1800 Rthl könne Świniary gerettet werden. Er will dann einen Teil seiner Güter dismembrieren, den Kindern die Zinsen zum Unterhalt anweisen und zum König gehen. Ohne Hilfe gehe er nach Königsberg. Mit Hilfe könne er am 12. Sept. abreisen und am 16. in Sławięcice sein.

reading.notes: A distraught letter signed v Triebenfeld (the sender is recorded as not identified) to a Hoffrath who is not named and is now in Breslau. The writer needs 1800 rt of interest to be paid. The v. d. Lahr affair has disgraced him, and his estates, including Schweinern, have been sequestered. He begs the recipient to get the Fürst to pay. His plan: sell off part of his estates, settle the interest on his children and go to the King. If no help comes, he will go to Königsberg. With help he could leave on 12 Sept and be in Schlawenschitz by the 16th. Nothing about Trąbczyn.
